2KI.1.1-2.text: Ahaziah is hurt and asks Baal-zebub if he will live

2KI.1.3-4.text: An angel sends Elijah to say Ahaziah will die

2KI.1.5-6.text: The messengers tell Ahaziah what Elijah said

2KI.1.7-8.text: Ahaziah learns that the man was Elijah

2KI.1.9-10.text: Fire from heaven kills the first captain and his men

2KI.1.11-12.text: Fire from heaven kills a second captain and his men

2KI.1.13-14.text: The third captain begs Elijah to spare his life

2KI.1.15-16.text: Elijah tells King Ahaziah he will surely die

2KI.2.1-2.text: Elisha refuses to leave Elijah and goes to Bethel

2KI.2.3-4.text: Elisha stays with Elijah on the way to Jericho

2KI.2.5-6.text: Elisha stays with Elijah on the way to the Jordan

2KI.2.7-8.text: Elijah parts the Jordan River and crosses with Elisha

2KI.2.9-10.text: Elisha asks Elijah for a double portion of his spirit

2KI.2.11-12.text: Elijah goes up to heaven in a whirlwind

2KI.2.13-14.text: Elisha takes Elijah’s cloak and parts the Jordan

2KI.2.15-16.text: The prophets bow to Elisha and want to search for Elijah

2KI.2.17-18.text: Elisha sends fifty men who do not find Elijah

check.why: The prophets sent the men to search for Elijah, not Elisha, who had warned them not to go.
check.suggestion: Fifty men search for Elijah but do not find him

2KI.2.19-20.text: The men of Jericho tell Elisha the water is bad

2KI.2.21-22.text: Elisha puts salt in the spring and heals the water

2KI.3.1-3.text: Jehoram becomes king of Israel and does evil

2KI.3.4-6.text: Moab rebels, and King Jehoram gathers Israel’s army

2KI.3.7-8.text: Jehoshaphat agrees to join Jehoram against Moab

2KI.3.9-10.text: The three kings run out of water in the desert

2KI.3.11-12.text: The three kings go to ask Elisha for God’s word

2KI.3.13-14.text: Elisha speaks harshly to Jehoram but honors Jehoshaphat

2KI.3.15-17.text: Elisha says God will fill the valley with water

2KI.3.18-19.text: Elisha says God will give Moab to the three kings

2KI.3.20-20.text: Water flows from Edom and fills the land

2KI.3.21-23.text: The Moabites see red water and think it is blood

2KI.3.24-25.text: Israel defeats Moab and destroys the land

2KI.3.26-27.text: Moab’s king offers his son and Israel goes home

2KI.4.1-2.text: A prophet’s widow asks Elisha for help with her debt

2KI.4.3-4.text: Elisha tells the widow to borrow many empty jars

2KI.4.5-6.text: The widow pours oil into jars until all are full

2KI.4.7-7.text: Elisha tells the widow to sell the oil and pay her debt

2KI.4.8-9.text: A woman in Shunem feeds Elisha and calls him holy

2KI.4.10-11.text: The Shunammite woman makes a small room for Elisha

2KI.4.12-13.text: Elisha offers to help the woman, but she needs nothing

2KI.4.14-16.text: Elisha promises the woman she will have a son

2KI.4.17-17.text: The woman gives birth to a son, as Elisha said

2KI.4.18-20.text: The Shunammite’s son gets a headache and dies

2KI.4.21-22.text: The mother asks her husband for a donkey to go to Elisha

2KI.4.23-24.text: The husband questions her trip, but she says all is well

2KI.4.25-26.text: Elisha sends Gehazi to ask the woman if all is well

2KI.4.27-27.text: Elisha stops Gehazi from pushing the woman away

2KI.4.28-29.text: Elisha sends Gehazi with his staff to the boy

2KI.4.30-31.text: Gehazi’s staff does not wake the boy

check.why: The staff belonged to Elisha, not to Gehazi.
check.suggestion: Elisha’s staff does not wake the boy

2KI.4.32-34.text: Elisha prays and lies on the dead boy, who becomes warm

2KI.4.35-37.text: The boy comes alive and Elisha gives him to his mother

2KI.4.38-39.text: A man puts unknown wild gourds into the stew pot

2KI.4.40-41.text: Elisha puts flour in the pot and the stew is safe

2KI.5.1-2.text: Naaman is a great commander with leprosy

2KI.5.3-4.text: An Israelite girl says a prophet can cure Naaman

2KI.5.5-6.text: The king of Aram sends Naaman to Israel with a letter

2KI.5.7-7.text: The king of Israel is upset by the letter

2KI.5.8-10.text: Elisha tells Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan

2KI.5.11-12.text: Naaman is angry about washing in the Jordan

2KI.5.13-14.text: Naaman’s servants persuade him, and he is made clean

2KI.5.15-16.text: Naaman praises God, but Elisha refuses his gift

2KI.5.17-19.text: Naaman asks for soil and for God’s forgiveness

2KI.5.20-22.text: Gehazi runs after Naaman and lies to get silver

2KI.5.23-25.text: Gehazi hides the gifts and lies to Elisha

2KI.5.26-27.text: Elisha says Gehazi will have Naaman’s leprosy

2KI.6.1-3.text: The prophets ask to build a bigger place at the Jordan

2KI.6.4-5.text: A man loses a borrowed axe head in the Jordan

2KI.6.6-7.text: Elisha makes the iron axe head float

2KI.6.8-9.text: Elisha warns the king of Israel about Aram’s camp

2KI.6.10-11.text: The king of Aram is angry about Elisha’s warnings

2KI.6.12-13.text: A servant tells the king that Elisha knows his plans

2KI.6.14-16.text: Aram’s army surrounds the city, but Elisha tells his servant not to fear

check.why: At 72 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: Elisha tells his servant not to fear the Aramean army

2KI.6.17-19.text: Elisha’s servant sees God’s army; Elisha leads the blinded Arameans to Samaria

check.why: At 79 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: God blinds the Arameans, and Elisha leads them to Samaria

2KI.6.20-21.text: God opens the Arameans’ eyes in Samaria; the king asks Elisha what to do

check.why: At 73 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: God opens the Arameans’ eyes; the king asks to kill them

2KI.6.22-23.text: Elisha tells the king to feed the Arameans and send them home

check.why: At 61 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: The king feeds the Arameans and sends them home

2KI.6.24-26.text: Aram besieges Samaria and a terrible famine begins

2KI.6.27-29.text: A woman tells the king about the boiled son

2KI.6.30-31.text: The king tears his clothes and vows to kill Elisha

2KI.6.32-33.text: Elisha tells the elders to keep the king’s messenger out

2KI.7.3-4.text: Four men with leprosy decide to go to the Aramean camp

2KI.7.5-6.text: The four men find the Aramean camp empty

2KI.7.7-8.text: The four men eat in the empty camp and hide the treasure

2KI.7.9-11.text: The four men decide to tell the king’s household the news

2KI.7.12-13.text: The king fears a trap, but a servant suggests sending scouts

2KI.7.14-15.text: The scouts follow the Arameans and find clothing along the road

check.why: At 63 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: Scouts track the Arameans and find abandoned clothes

2KI.7.16-17.text: The people plunder the camp, and the officer is trampled to death

check.why: At 65 characters, the title exceeds the 60-character limit.
check.suggestion: The people plunder the camp, and the officer is trampled

2KI.7.18-20.text: Elisha’s words come true for the doubting officer

2KI.8.1-2.text: Elisha tells the Shunammite woman to leave because of famine

2KI.8.3-4.text: The woman returns and goes to the king for her land

2KI.8.5-6.text: Gehazi tells the king about her; the king restores her land

2KI.8.7-9.text: Ben-hadad sends Hazael to ask Elisha if he will recover

2KI.8.10-12.text: Elisha tells Hazael that Ben-hadad will die and weeps

2KI.8.13-15.text: Hazael kills Ben-hadad and becomes king of Aram

2KI.8.18-19.text: Jehoram does evil, but God keeps his promise to David

2KI.8.20-21.text: Edom rebels against Judah and Jehoram’s troops flee

2KI.8.22-24.text: Edom and Libnah stay in revolt, and Jehoram dies

2KI.8.25-27.text: Ahaziah becomes king of Judah and does evil

2KI.8.28-29.text: Ahaziah visits the wounded King Joram at Jezreel

2KI.9.1-3.text: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu as king

2KI.9.4-6.text: The young prophet anoints Jehu king over Israel

2KI.9.7-8.text: God tells Jehu to destroy the house of Ahab

2KI.9.9-10.text: The prophet says Jezebel will die; then he runs away

2KI.9.11-13.text: Jehu’s fellow officers proclaim him king

2KI.9.14-16.text: Jehu plots against Joram and goes to Jezreel

2KI.9.17-18.text: Joram’s first rider meets Jehu and does not return

2KI.9.19-20.text: A second rider goes to Jehu and does not return

2KI.9.21-22.text: Joram and Ahaziah meet Jehu at Naboth’s field

2KI.9.23-24.text: Jehu shoots Joram with an arrow and kills him

2KI.9.25-26.text: Jehu orders Joram’s body thrown into Naboth’s field

2KI.9.27-28.text: Ahaziah of Judah is shot and dies at Megiddo

2KI.9.29-29.text: Ahaziah became king of Judah in Joram’s eleventh year

2KI.9.30-32.text: Jezebel challenges Jehu from her window

2KI.9.33-34.text: Jehu has Jezebel thrown down from the window

2KI.9.35-37.text: Only parts of Jezebel are found, as Elijah said

2KI.10.1-3.text: Jehu writes to Samaria’s leaders about Ahab’s sons

2KI.10.4-5.text: Samaria’s leaders promise to obey Jehu

2KI.10.6-7.text: Samaria’s leaders kill Ahab’s seventy sons for Jehu

2KI.10.8-9.text: Jehu shows the heads and speaks to the people

2KI.10.10-11.text: Jehu kills the rest of Ahab’s house in Jezreel

2KI.10.12-14.text: Jehu kills forty-two relatives of Ahaziah

2KI.10.15-17.text: Jehu meets Jehonadab and destroys Ahab’s family

2KI.10.18-20.text: Jehu pretends he will serve Baal and calls an assembly

2KI.10.21-22.text: All the servants of Baal gather in the temple of Baal

2KI.10.23-24.text: Jehu checks that only servants of Baal are in the temple

2KI.10.25-27.text: Jehu’s men kill Baal’s servants and destroy the temple

2KI.10.28-28.text: Jehu removes the worship of Baal from Israel

2KI.10.29-31.text: Jehu keeps the sins of Jeroboam despite God’s promise

2KI.10.32-33.text: Hazael takes land from Israel east of the Jordan

2KI.11.4-6.text: Jehoiada makes a covenant with the commanders

2KI.11.7-8.text: Jehoiada tells the guards to protect the king

2KI.11.9-10.text: The commanders obey Jehoiada and receive David’s weapons

2KI.11.11-12.text: Jehoiada crowns Joash king and the people cheer

2KI.11.13-14.text: Athaliah sees the king and cries out that it is treason

2KI.11.15-16.text: Athaliah is taken out and put to death

2KI.11.17-18.text: Jehoiada makes a covenant and the people end Baal worship

2KI.11.19-20.text: Joash sits on the throne and the people rejoice

2KI.11.21-21.text: Joash becomes king at seven years old

2KI.12.1-3.text: Joash does right, but the high places remain

2KI.12.4-5.text: Joash tells the priests to use temple money for repairs

2KI.12.6-8.text: Joash rebukes the priests for not repairing the temple

2KI.12.9-10.text: Jehoiada sets a money chest beside the altar

2KI.12.11-12.text: Counted money pays the workers and buys materials

check.why: The supervisors pay the workers and buy materials, not the money itself.
check.suggestion: Supervisors use the money to pay workers and buy materials

2KI.12.13-14.text: The money is used for repairs, not for temple articles

2KI.12.15-16.text: Honest men pay the workers; offering money is for priests

2KI.12.17-18.text: Joash pays Hazael with temple gold to save Jerusalem

2KI.12.19-21.text: Servants kill Joash, and his son Amaziah becomes king

2KI.13.1-2.text: Jehoahaz becomes king of Israel and does evil

2KI.13.3-5.text: The LORD hears Jehoahaz and sends Israel a deliverer

2KI.13.6-7.text: Israel keeps sinning, and Jehoahaz has a small army

2KI.13.8-9.text: Jehoahaz dies, and his son Jehoash becomes king

2KI.13.10-11.text: Jehoash becomes king of Israel and does evil

2KI.13.12-13.text: Jehoash dies, and Jeroboam becomes king of Israel

2KI.13.14-16.text: Jehoash visits sick Elisha and takes a bow and arrows

2KI.13.17-19.text: Elisha says Jehoash will defeat Aram three times

2KI.13.20-21.text: A dead man comes alive when he touches Elisha’s bones

2KI.13.22-25.text: The LORD is kind to Israel, and Jehoash defeats Aram

2KI.14.1-3.text: Amaziah becomes king and does right, but not like David

2KI.14.4-5.text: Amaziah executes the servants who killed his father

2KI.14.6-7.text: Amaziah spares the murderers’ sons and defeats Edom

2KI.14.8-10.text: Jehoash warns Amaziah not to fight

2KI.14.13-14.text: Jehoash captures Amaziah and takes Jerusalem’s treasures

2KI.14.20-20.text: Amaziah is buried in Jerusalem with his fathers

2KI.14.23-25.text: Jeroboam II becomes king and restores Israel’s border

2KI.14.26-27.text: The LORD sees Israel’s suffering and saves Israel

2KI.14.28-29.text: Jeroboam dies, and his son Zechariah becomes king

2KI.15.1-3.text: Azariah becomes king of Judah and does right

2KI.15.4-5.text: The LORD afflicts Azariah with leprosy; Jotham governs

2KI.15.6-7.text: Azariah dies and his son Jotham becomes king

2KI.15.8-9.text: Zechariah rules Israel six months and does evil

2KI.15.10-12.text: Shallum kills Zechariah and becomes king of Israel

2KI.15.13-14.text: Menahem kills Shallum and becomes king of Israel

2KI.15.15-16.text: Menahem cruelly attacks the people of Tiphsah

2KI.15.17-18.text: Menahem rules Israel ten years and does evil

2KI.15.19-20.text: Menahem pays the king of Assyria to leave Israel

2KI.15.21-22.text: Menahem dies and his son Pekahiah becomes king

2KI.15.23-24.text: Pekahiah rules Israel two years and does evil

2KI.15.25-26.text: Pekah kills Pekahiah and becomes king of Israel

2KI.15.27-28.text: Pekah rules Israel twenty years and does evil

2KI.15.29-31.text: Assyria captures cities, and Hoshea kills Pekah

2KI.15.32-33.text: Jotham becomes king of Judah at age twenty-five

2KI.15.34-38.text: Jotham does right, but the people still use high places

2KI.16.1-2.text: Ahaz becomes king of Judah and does not follow David

check.why: The text states that Ahaz did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, not that he did not follow David.
check.suggestion: Ahaz becomes king of Judah and does not do what is right

2KI.16.3-4.text: Ahaz sacrifices his son and worships at high places

2KI.16.5-6.text: Aram and Israel attack Jerusalem; Aram takes Elath

2KI.16.7-9.text: Ahaz sends silver and gold to Assyria for help

2KI.16.10-12.text: Ahaz has Uriah build a new altar like one in Damascus

2KI.16.13-14.text: Ahaz offers on the new altar and moves the bronze altar

2KI.16.15-16.text: Ahaz orders Uriah to use the new altar for offerings

2KI.16.17-18.text: Ahaz changes parts of the temple because of Assyria

2KI.16.19-20.text: Ahaz dies and his son Hezekiah becomes king

2KI.17.1-3.text: Hoshea becomes king of Israel and pays tribute to Assyria

2KI.17.4-4.text: The king of Assyria puts Hoshea in prison

2KI.17.5-6.text: Assyria captures Samaria and takes the Israelites away

2KI.17.7-8.text: The Israelites sinned by worshiping other gods

2KI.17.9-10.text: The Israelites secretly built high places and idols

2KI.17.11-12.text: The Israelites burned incense and served idols

2KI.17.13-13.text: The LORD warns Israel and Judah through the prophets

2KI.17.14-15.text: The Israelites refuse to listen and follow worthless idols

2KI.17.16-18.text: The LORD removes Israel because of idols and evil

2KI.17.19-20.text: Judah also disobeys and the LORD punishes Israel

2KI.17.21-23.text: The LORD removed Israel because of Jeroboam’s sins

2KI.17.24-26.text: Foreigners settle in Samaria, and lions kill some

2KI.17.27-28.text: The king of Assyria sends a priest to teach the settlers

2KI.17.29-31.text: Each nation of settlers makes its own idols in Samaria

2KI.17.32-33.text: The settlers worship the LORD and also serve other gods

2KI.17.34-35.text: The settlers keep old customs and do not obey the LORD

2KI.17.36-38.text: The LORD told Israel to worship only him

2KI.17.39-41.text: The settlers do not listen and keep serving idols

2KI.18.1-3.text: Hezekiah becomes king of Judah and does what is right

2KI.18.4-5.text: Hezekiah removes idols and trusts the LORD

2KI.18.6-8.text: The LORD is with Hezekiah, who rebels against Assyria

2KI.18.9-10.text: Assyria captures Samaria after three years

2KI.18.11-12.text: Assyria exiles Israel because Israel disobeyed the LORD

2KI.18.13-15.text: Hezekiah pays Sennacherib to leave Judah

2KI.18.16-16.text: Hezekiah gives the temple gold to Assyria’s king

2KI.18.17-18.text: Assyria’s officers meet Hezekiah’s officials at Jerusalem

2KI.18.19-21.text: The Rabshakeh mocks Hezekiah’s trust in Egypt

2KI.18.22-23.text: The Rabshakeh mocks trust in the LORD and offers horses

2KI.18.24-25.text: The Rabshakeh says the LORD sent Assyria against Judah

2KI.18.26-27.text: Hezekiah’s officials ask the Rabshakeh to speak Aramaic

2KI.18.28-30.text: The Rabshakeh tells the people not to trust Hezekiah

2KI.18.31-32.text: The Rabshakeh urges the people to surrender to Assyria

2KI.18.33-35.text: The Rabshakeh says no god has saved a land from Assyria

2KI.18.36-37.text: The people stay silent, and officials report to Hezekiah

2KI.19.1-2.text: Hezekiah goes to the temple and sends men to Isaiah

2KI.19.3-4.text: Hezekiah asks Isaiah to pray for the remnant

2KI.19.5-7.text: Isaiah tells Hezekiah not to be afraid of Assyria

2KI.19.8-9.text: Sennacherib sends messengers to Hezekiah again

2KI.19.10-11.text: Sennacherib warns Hezekiah not to trust God

2KI.19.12-13.text: Sennacherib says the gods of other nations failed

2KI.19.14-15.text: Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD and prays

2KI.19.16-18.text: Hezekiah asks the LORD to hear Sennacherib’s words

2KI.19.19-19.text: Hezekiah asks the LORD to save Judah

2KI.19.20-22.text: Isaiah tells Hezekiah that God heard his prayer

2KI.19.23-24.text: God says Sennacherib mocked him and boasted of his power

2KI.19.25-26.text: God says he planned long ago what Assyria has done

2KI.19.27-28.text: God will turn Sennacherib back with a hook in his nose

2KI.19.29-31.text: God gives Hezekiah a sign that Judah will live and grow

2KI.19.32-34.text: God promises that Assyria’s king will not enter Jerusalem

2KI.20.1-3.text: Isaiah tells sick Hezekiah he will die, and Hezekiah prays

2KI.20.4-5.text: God tells Isaiah to say he will heal Hezekiah

2KI.20.6-7.text: God adds fifteen years to Hezekiah’s life and heals him

2KI.20.8-9.text: Hezekiah asks Isaiah for a sign that God will heal him

2KI.20.10-11.text: Isaiah prays and the shadow goes back ten steps

2KI.20.12-13.text: Hezekiah shows the Babylonian envoys all his treasures

2KI.20.14-15.text: Isaiah asks Hezekiah about the men from Babylon

2KI.20.16-18.text: Isaiah says Babylon will take away Hezekiah’s treasures

2KI.20.19-19.text: Hezekiah accepts Isaiah’s word and hopes for peace

2KI.21.1-3.text: Manasseh becomes king and does evil like the nations

2KI.21.4-6.text: Manasseh builds altars to false gods in the temple

2KI.21.7-9.text: Manasseh sets an Asherah pole in the temple

2KI.21.10-12.text: God says he will bring disaster on Jerusalem and Judah

2KI.21.13-15.text: God says he will wipe out Jerusalem like a bowl

2KI.21.16-18.text: Manasseh kills many innocent people and then dies

2KI.21.19-20.text: Amon becomes king of Judah and does evil

2KI.21.21-23.text: Amon follows his father’s idols and his servants kill him

2KI.21.24-26.text: The people make Josiah king after Amon dies

2KI.22.3-5.text: Josiah tells Shaphan to have the temple money counted

2KI.22.6-7.text: The money is given to workers who repair the temple

check.why: These verses continue Josiah’s speech directing that the workers need not account for the money, rather than describing the money being given.
check.suggestion: Josiah says the temple workers need not account for money

2KI.22.8-10.text: Hilkiah finds the Book of the Law and Shaphan reads it

2KI.22.11-13.text: Josiah tears his clothes and sends men to ask God

2KI.22.14-16.text: Huldah says God will bring disaster on Jerusalem

2KI.22.17-19.text: Huldah says God heard Josiah because he humbled himself

2KI.22.20-20.text: Huldah says Josiah will die in peace

2KI.23.1-2.text: Josiah reads the Book of the Covenant to all the people

2KI.23.3-3.text: Josiah and the people make a covenant to follow the LORD

check.why: Words in sentence case should not be written in all-capital letters.
check.suggestion: Josiah and the people make a covenant to follow the Lord

2KI.23.4-5.text: Josiah removes Baal objects and idol priests

2KI.23.6-7.text: Josiah burns the Asherah pole and tears down shrine rooms

2KI.23.8-9.text: Josiah destroys the high places across Judah

2KI.23.10-11.text: Josiah ends child sacrifice and removes the sun horses

2KI.23.12-14.text: Josiah destroys altars and high places built by kings

2KI.23.15-16.text: Josiah destroys the Bethel altar and burns bones on it

2KI.23.17-18.text: Josiah leaves the tomb of the man of God alone

2KI.23.19-20.text: Josiah removes shrines in Samaria and returns to Jerusalem

2KI.23.21-23.text: Josiah commands the people to keep the Passover

2KI.23.24-25.text: Josiah removes mediums and idols and obeys the Law

2KI.23.26-27.text: The LORD is still angry with Judah because of Manasseh

2KI.23.31-33.text: Jehoahaz reigns three months and Pharaoh Neco imprisons him

2KI.23.34-35.text: Pharaoh Neco makes Eliakim king and renames him Jehoiakim

2KI.24.1-2.text: Nebuchadnezzar invades and Jehoiakim later rebels

2KI.24.3-4.text: The LORD sends this trouble because of Manasseh’s sins

check.why: The reference in “this trouble” is not clear when read alone in a list.
check.suggestion: The LORD removes Judah because of Manasseh’s sins

2KI.24.5-5.text: The rest of Jehoiakim’s acts are in the royal records

2KI.24.6-6.text: Jehoiakim dies and his son Jehoiachin becomes king

2KI.24.7-7.text: Babylon’s king takes the land of the king of Egypt

2KI.24.8-9.text: Jehoiachin becomes king at eighteen and does evil

2KI.24.10-12.text: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem and takes Jehoiachin

2KI.24.13-14.text: Nebuchadnezzar takes the temple treasures and many captives

2KI.24.15-17.text: Nebuchadnezzar exiles Jehoiachin and makes Zedekiah king

2KI.25.1-3.text: Nebuchadnezzar surrounds Jerusalem and famine grows

2KI.25.4-5.text: The city wall is broken and Zedekiah flees but is caught

2KI.25.6-7.text: Babylon’s soldiers kill Zedekiah’s sons and blind him

2KI.25.8-10.text: Nebuzaradan burns the temple, palace and houses

2KI.25.11-12.text: Nebuzaradan exiles the people but leaves the poorest

2KI.25.13-15.text: The Chaldeans take the temple’s bronze, gold and silver

2KI.25.16-17.text: The size of the temple’s bronze pillars is described

2KI.25.18-19.text: Nebuzaradan takes the chief priest and other leaders

2KI.25.20-21.text: The king of Babylon kills the leaders at Riblah

2KI.25.27-27.text: Evil-merodach releases King Jehoiachin from prison

2KI.25.28-30.text: The king of Babylon is kind to Jehoiachin and feeds him
